record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For the two-dimensional Lieb-Thirring constants as γ→0+, determine the asymptotic behavior of L_{γ,2}, and decide whether L_{γ,2} and the one-particle constant L^(1)_{γ,2} have the same leading-order constant in that limit.

evidence.quote: Probably, both Lγ,2 and L(1)γ,2 behave like a constant times γ−1. Are the two constants the same?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}$ be a real-valued potential with $V_-=\max(-V,0)\in L^{\gamma+1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$, where $\gamma>0$. Consider the Schrödinger operator $-\Delta+V$ acting in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$, and let $\{-\lambda_j(V)\}_{j\ge 1}$ denote its negative eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity). Define the sharp Lieb–Thirring constant in dimension two by
$$L_{\gamma,2}\;=\;\sup_{V}\;\frac{\sum_{j}\lambda_j(V)^{\gamma}}{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} V_-(x)^{\gamma+1}\,dx},$$
the supremum being over all admissible non-trivial $V$, and define the one-particle (one-bound-state) constant $L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}$ by the analogous supremum but with the numerator replaced by $\lambda_1(V)^\gamma$ (the $\gamma$th power of the lowest eigenvalue alone):
$$L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}\;=\;\sup_{V}\;\frac{\lambda_1(V)^\gamma}{\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb{R}^2} V_-(x)^{\gamma+1}\,dx}.$$

(a) Determine the asymptotic behavior of $L_{\gamma,2}$ as $\gamma\to 0^+$. In particular, prove or disprove that there is a constant $c>0$ with
$$L_{\gamma,2}\;\sim\;c\,\gamma^{-1}\qquad(\gamma\to 0^+),$$
and similarly identify the leading-order behavior of $L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}$.

(b) Decide whether the leading-order constants of $L_{\gamma,2}$ and $L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}$ coincide as $\gamma\to 0^+$, i.e.\ whether
$$\lim_{\gamma\to 0^+}\frac{L_{\gamma,2}}{L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}}\;=\;1.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys of Lieb–Thirring inequalities (including the 2022 update on the state of the Lieb–Thirring inequality) continue to list the sharp value of $L_{\gamma,2}$ for small $\gamma>0$ as unresolved, and the question of whether $L_{\gamma,2}$ and $L^{(1)}_{\gamma,2}$ share the same leading constant as $\gamma\to 0^+$ does not appear to have been settled. No definitive resolution was found in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture (arXiv:2203.06051)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing sharp Lieb–Thirring constants, including the two-dimensional case where the constants are known only for very limited ranges of γ.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp values and small-γ asymptotics of L_{γ,2} remain open in the recent survey literature.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring inequality — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In two dimensions the inequality holds iff γ>0; sharp constants are known only in special cases.
status_evidence.claim: The sharp two-dimensional constants are not generally known, particularly as γ→0+.
